extracted.intended_audience: creative writers, literary critics, students of literature, and short-story writers interested in aesthetic theory
extracted.subtask_description: Use Sontag's 'Against Interpretation' as a rubric for judging or revising fiction: prioritize sensory presence, surface, and form over extracting intellectual meaning or allegory. Focus on what the text does on the page (sentences, images, rhythms) rather than what it 'means.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Against interpretation (anti-interpretive impulse)
rubrics_metrics.description: The contemporary critical impulse to ask 'what does it mean?' is a flight from the actual sensory presence of the work; interpretation reduces art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reducing a work to paraphraseable 'content' or message. Treat attempts to translate art into intellectual meaning as evasion of its sensory effects ('flight from the actual sensory presence of the work'). The guiding slogan: 'In place of a hermeneutics we need an erotics of art.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Form is content
rubrics_metrics.description: The artificial separation of form and content has impoverished criticism; form is itself the content of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate style, surface, sentence-level choices, rhythms, and formal devices as carriers of meaning rather than as ornamentation to be peeled away. Anti-pattern: treating form as secondary to an underlying 'real meaning.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparence (experience the thing itself)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Transparence is the highest, most liberating value in art and in criticism today." Transparence means experiencing the luminousness of the thing in itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A successful work allows itself to be seen rather than decoded; criticism ought to enable direct, luminous experience of the work. Scoring note: prioritize works that foreground immediate perception over symbolic decoding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Against allegory
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern criticism's tendency to treat every work as an allegory for something else (Freud, Marx, biography, history) is reductive; the work is not a clue to a hidden truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not interpret every element as standing for a psychological, political, or biographical 'meaning.' Anti-patterns include defaulting to Freudian, Marxist, biographical, or historical allegorizing that eclipses surface presence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sensory engagement / erotic response
rubrics_metrics.description: Aesthetic experience is bodily, immediate, erotic; the critic or reader should respond with sensation rather than only with intellectual abstraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value works that provoke bodily, immediate reactions—images, textures, sounds, and physical responses—over those that invite only abstract analysis. Warning: intellectual insulation from the work (treating it as merely data for interpretation) is a mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camp: privileging artifice and surface
rubrics_metrics.description: Camp as a sensibility privileges artifice, exaggeration, and surface over depth, validating aesthetic responses outside high-modernist seriousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and legitimize works that employ artifice, theatricality, and exaggeration as deliberate aesthetic strategies rather than lapses from 'serious' art. Scoring note: surface effects and deliberate artifice can be virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resists easy interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: A work of art succeeds when it resists being readily paraphrased or reduced to a single, easy interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-scoring works should thwart reductive summary; ambiguity, complexity of surface, and refusal to yield a simple message count positively. Anti-pattern: works that read as thinly allegorical or didactic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintains sensory intensity
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful work sustains sensory intensity across its surface—images, tones, and formal textures remain vivid and present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess continuity and strength of sensory detail and affect throughout the piece. Works that flatten into mere idea-statements or dry exposition lose points for lack of sensory force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency as the work itself (not a coded message)
rubrics_metrics.description: The work should be the 'thing itself' rather than a coded message to be decoded; transparency is an aesthetic achievement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer pieces that present themselves plainly as experiences rather than as puzzles to be solved. Criticism should aim to reveal the work's luminous surface rather than to unmask hidden content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privileges form (formal achievement over didactic content)
rubrics_metrics.description: The work should privilege formal accomplishment—sentencecraft, structure, voice—because form is where meaning resides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate technical mastery (sentence-level craft, pacing, structural choices) as primary. Penalize pieces that trade formal inventiveness for straightforward moralizing or message delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permits an erotic, not merely intellectual, response
rubrics_metrics.description: A valuable artwork invites erotic (bodily, affective) responses in addition to, or instead of, purely intellectual reactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rate works by their capacity to move the reader bodily or sensually; pieces that solicit only cerebral assent should be rated lower under this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: What fiction does on the page (sentences, images, rhythms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiction should be judged by what it performs materially on the page—its sentences, images, and rhythms—rather than by its conveyed 'meaning.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or revising fiction, focus feedback on concrete textual effects (line-level music, imagery, cadence, sensory detail). Heed Sontag's warning: 'Fiction reduced to message is fiction destroyed.'
